messages.author: 4d1bbaec1f0d1dfe
messages.subject: Eigenvector of divergence (d)
parts:
Hi all,

I am experiencing some difficulties in calculating divergence vectors (d) following Langerhans (2009 J Evol Biol - attached), and any help would be greatly appreciated.

d describes the linear combination of dependent variables with the greatest difference in Euclidean space between treatments (in my case, predation regimes), while statistically controlling for other terms in the MANCOVA model. Langerhans (page 1061) performs a PCA of H (Sums of Squares and Cross-Products [SSCP] matrix of the term of interest) to derive an eigenvector of divergence (d) in shape between treatments. 

Has anyone calculated this metric based on the functions implemented in geomorph? Any suggestions or ideas would be very welcome.

Thanks a lot,
Cheers
raul

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Eigenvector of divergence (d)
parts:
Raol,

 

This cannot be implemented in geomorph. Also, I would not recommend the procedure for evaluating trends in multivariate data. The procedure is basically one that forces multivariate data to a number line, and then performs statistics on those values. Such methods are well-known to identify patterns that don’t exist, or not find patterns that do exist.

 

Essentially, the values ‘d’ are one-dimensional projections in a space described by the independent variables, not the actual data. Then, this is used in the ancova. But differences among groups are not guaranteed to align with the first PC axis of the H-matrix: which is how ‘d’ is derived. 

 

This convoluted algebra (forcing multivariate data to a single dimension for further analysis) is also unnecessary. Divergence between groups (which is what the divergence vector ‘d’ attempts to describe), may be estimated directly in the full multivariate space. The function pairwise does this for example. Then, one may statistically compare these using RRPP and associated Z-scores.

 

Dean

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Eigenvector of divergence (d)
parts:
Raul,

You can get SSCPs using RRPP::manova.update on a procD.lm object.  You can perform eigen-analysis on these vectors, and data projections might give you some useful visual tools for visualizing, e.g., shape change associated with an effect.

I must warn you though against following the methods of that paper from that point on.  If you use the projected scores as data in other analyses, as that paper does, you introduce not only a circular line of reasoning into your data analysis, but strictly a bias, that renders the results unworthy of trust.

The divergence scores — data projected onto d — are scores that maximize a difference between treatments, irrespective of noise or other effects, that if used univariately are sure to find a treatment difference, because that is what you set out to do by calculating d.  This makes absolutely no sense.  Think about it, one is aligning a vector that best characterizes differences between groups and then asking if those groups are different, only along the vector where they were made to be most different.

The reason you cannot do this directly in geomorph is because it is asinine to do.  You can acquire the parts but your own assembly is required.

Best,
Mike
